question: Who built the ‘Shahi’ road connecting Indus Valley to Sonar Valley?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sher Shah Suri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sher Shah Suri** was the founder of the Suri Empire in India.
 
• He ruled from 1540 to 1545 after defeating the Mughal Emperor Humayun.
 
• Sher Shah Suri is known for his administrative reforms and development of infrastructure, including the construction of roads and inns.
 
• The 'Shahi' road, which connected the Indus Valley to the Sonar Valley, was one of his significant contributions to the empire's infrastructure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus Valley Civilization:**

 
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization, also known as the Harappan Civilization, was a Bronze Age civilization in the northwestern regions of South Asia.
 
• It was one of the world's earliest urban cultures, known for its advanced cities, trade, and crafts.
 
• Major sites include Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, and Dholavira.
 
 
 
• **Sher Shah Suri's Administrative Reforms:**
 
 
• Sher Shah Suri introduced several administrative reforms that influenced later Mughal administration.
 
• He improved the revenue system, introduced a new currency (the Rupiya), and standardized weights and measures.
 
• His reforms helped in the efficient management of the empire and the welfare of the people.
 
 
 
• **Suri Empire:**
 
 
• The Suri Empire was an Afghan dynasty that ruled northern India in the mid-16th century.
 
• It was established by Sher Shah Suri after he defeated the Mughal Emperor Humayun in 1540.
 
• The empire is known for its administrative and military strength as well as its contributions to architecture and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Grand Trunk Road:**
 
 
• The Grand Trunk Road is one of Asia's oldest and longest major roads, originally built by Sher Shah Suri.
 
• It runs from Chittagong in Bangladesh to Kabul in Afghanistan, covering a distance of about 2,500 kilometers.
 
• This road played a crucial role in facilitating trade and communication across the Indian subcontinent.
